pre_existing_not_this_lap.first_evidence: web/app/play/TracksPopover.tsx:111-124 -- `useAlphaTabEvent(api, 'scoreLoaded', (score) => { if (api?.score && api.score !== score) return; setSingleTrack(false); ...; setRenderedIndexes([]); multiDrawnRef.current = []; commitTracks(score.tracks.map((track) => toMixerTrack(track, engine?.model.Clef.G2, engine?.model.Clef.F4))); });` -- runs the full reset+rebuild unconditionally whenever `score` matches the live `api.score`, with no check for whether the mixer was already built for this exact score object.
pre_existing_not_this_lap.suggested_fix: Track the score the mixer was actually built for, in a ref matching this file's existing tracksRef/multiDrawnRef pattern, and skip the reset+rebuild when scoreLoaded fires again for that same object: `const mixerScoreRef = useRef<AlphaTab.model.Score | null>(null);` then inside the handler, after the existing identity guard: `if (mixerScoreRef.current === score) return; mixerScoreRef.current = score;` before the setSingleTrack/setRenderedIndexes/commitTracks calls. Naming the assumption: comparing `score` by reference is safe because NotationSurface's re-assert always replays the exact OpenNotation.score object already held in PlayerShell's `notation` state (see NotationSurface.tsx's renderOpenNotation), never a freshly re-parsed one -- so `===` correctly distinguishes 'the same score, reloaded' from 'a genuinely new score'.

residual_risks_unioned: NOT raised as a finding because it is documented as deferred, but confirmed live: TracksPopover.tsx:260 calls `api?.player?.resetChannelStates()` on every playerReady, and the pinned engine's Synthesizer.resetChannelStates (alphaTab.core.mjs:38911-38916) also does `this.applyTranspositionPitches(new Map())`, wiping the MAIN transposition map that `loadMidiForScore` had just handed over as the whole audio story (:46732-46742, built at :43010-43017 from `-track.staves[0].transpositionPitch`). The handler's re-assert loop restores volume, mute, solo and the LIVE audio transposition only, so a file carrying its own `\transpose` plays untransposed against the notation it is drawn at. docs/plans/2026-09-13-v0c-popovers-plan.md records this exactly ("Tracked separately; nothing re-asserts it today") — but it names no ticket, and this PR is the one that made the file's own transposition visible in the row, so the audio half now visibly disagrees with what the row says.

`transposeStart` (mixer-tracks.ts:83-86) reads `staves[0]` only, on the stated ground that a track whose staves disagree "cannot happen through this app". It can arrive from a FILE: the GP importer writes per staff (`staff.transpositionPitch = staffLayout.transpose`, alphaTab.core.mjs:17154). Such a track would be mis-reported by the row, and the first edit would flatten the other staves, because the engine's applyPitchOffsets (:3694) writes EVERY staff of the track from the one array slot. I could not confirm any real file does this, so it is not raised.

TrackRow's Transpose notation slider is min -12 / max 12 (TrackRow.tsx:376-384) while `transposeFull` is now seeded from the file, which can carry a larger value. Base UI would then render a clamped thumb against an out-of-range `value`, and a nudge would commit the clamped number — silently narrowing the file's transposition. No fixture in the repo exercises a transposition beyond an octave.

`applyRendered`'s `if (picked.length === 0) return;` is now REACHABLE in the very window `liveDrawnIndexes()` was added for: with two tracks drawn, a second untick inside the redraw gap computes from the live single-track set and empties it, so the click is silently swallowed. The outcome is benign (the checkbox reverts on renderFinished) but the comment above it still says "Reaching here at all would be a bug."

For the fourteen `apply: 'midi'` rows the engine call is now deferred to a requestAnimationFrame, so a throw out of `loadMidiForScore` lands in a detached callback rather than `applyThenPersist`'s try/catch. The VALIDATING throw is `fillFromJson`'s and is still synchronous inside the guard, so the documented "ask the engine first" contract holds; only a rebuild-time throw would now escape and leave the value persisted.

Callsite completeness for SETTING_TEXT_VALIDATORS, SETTING_LABELS and `cancelQueuedFrames` is grep-only (no symbol-aware search in this harness), so "nothing else reads this map" is asserted from text search over web/ and client/ alone.

VERIFIED NEGATIVE — the font-shorthand injection defence holds at the engine's real sink, and the two gated paths are the only ways in. The sink is alphaTab.core.mjs:49768, `let s = `<text x="…" y="…" style='stroke: none; font:${this.font.toCssString(this.settings.display.scale)}; …'``, and it reaches the DOM through alphaTab.core.mjs:41210 `if (typeof body === "string") placeholder.innerHTML = body;` — an HTML-parser sink with a single-quoted attribute, exactly as the comment at settings-schema.ts:247-252 says. Refusing `'`, `<` and `>` closes the breakout: measured, a permitted `12px a"b` round-trips through Font.fromJson to the css string `12px a"b` (FontParser.quoteFont returns a space-free family RAW), and a double quote inside a single-quoted attribute is inert. `grep -rE 'dangerouslySetInnerHTML|innerHTML|insertAdjacentHTML|outerHTML|document\.write|new Function' web client/src tooling` returns one hit, client/src/main.tsx:26, and it is a read guard. And `display.resources.*Font` / `elementFonts.*` are named in exactly one file in web/ (settings-schema.ts); defaults.ts sets no font, no AlphaTab importer writes settings.display.resources (the only engine-side writer is alphaTab.core.mjs:40899, which assigns the engine's own bundled web-font family), and mergeAgainstDefaults iterates the DEFAULTS, so a stored key the defaults do not declare — any of the other elementFonts members, or smuflFontFamilyName — is dropped before the engine sees it. So the field validator plus SETTING_TEXT_VALIDATORS really are the only two paths, and the injection half is closed.

The validator permits `;`, which the sink does pass through: a stored `12px a;b` round-trips to the css string `12px a;b`, so the emitted attribute becomes `style='stroke: none; font:12px a; b; dominant-baseline: …'` — one extra CSS declaration on that one <text> element. No breakout (the `'` delimiter is refused) and nothing script-capable follows from a declaration on an SVG text node, so I am NOT filing it; recording it because a future change to how that buffer is consumed — an XML parse, a CSP report, a sanitizer — would make the boundary matter.

isCssColor is over-strict in one place and its doc comment is inaccurate about it: settings-schema.ts:219-220 claims 'Exactly the colour notations AlphaTab's own Color.fromJson parses: 3-, 6- or 8-digit hex', but Color.fromJson also accepts 4-digit #RGBA (alphaTab.core.mjs, the `json.length === 5` arm) — measured, Color.fromJson('#f00f') returns #FF0000 while isCssColor('#f00f') is false. Over-strict is the safe direction for the engine, but the restore path would REPAIR a legitimately stored #RGBA back to its default and toast about it. Correctness/copy, not security, so not filed as a security finding.

Reachability boundary for both findings: today the only writer of those keys is the app itself, and it writes well-formed values (the `color` rows come from `<input type="color">`, the `text` rows are trimmed on commit since ee592f98). So the triggers are a store written by something other than the current build — DevTools, a shared browser profile, an extension, a sync tool, an older build of this branch, or any XSS elsewhere on the origin. I found no XSS to bootstrap it from, which is why both sit at P2 rather than higher; they are the defence-in-depth the new repair path was added to BE, with five of six colour keys and every whitespace-padded value outside it.

No ReDoS in the new patterns. HEX_COLOR is a fixed-length alternation; RGB_COLOR's `\d+(?:\.\d+)?` and FONT_SIZE's `\d+(?:\.\d+)?(?:px|pt|em)` are both anchored with no nested quantifier, so a long digit run backtracks linearly (each retry fails `\.` against a digit immediately). replaceAll(/\s+/g,'') and split(/\s+/) are single linear passes. localStorage can hold megabytes, so this was worth checking.

settings-paths.ts is clean against prototype pollution and I could not break it: writeInto builds `{ ...base, [head]: … }`, and a computed key in an object literal uses CreateDataProperty, which never invokes the '__proto__' setter — the reasoning at settings-paths.ts:51-56 is correct. Independently, mergeAgainstDefaults iterates `Object.entries(defaults)`, so no key from the stored document ever becomes a write target.

Error copy is safe: everything interpolated into a message is either a hardcoded module constant (the `repaired` paths come from Object.entries over SETTING_OPTION_VALUES / SETTING_TEXT_VALIDATORS / SETTING_NUMERIC_BOUNDS, and SETTING_LABELS supplies their names) or a file name, and all of it lands in Sonner as a React child or in globalThis.confirm — `grep -rln dangerouslySetInnerHTML client/node_modules/sonner/dist/` is empty. The console.warn at PlayerShell.tsx:210 correctly uses a literal format string with the values as arguments. No secrets in the diff.

Not mine to file, flagging for the correctness lane: PlayerShell.tsx:668 builds `link.download = `${api.score.title || 'score'}.gp`` from a title parsed out of an opened file (untrusted content). Browsers sanitise the download attribute, so I could not construct a path-traversal or extension swap from it, and the line is untouched by this diff — but it is the one place file-derived text reaches a browser API rather than a React child.

assert-design-system-css.mjs: I ran the new `isWholeClass` against the real emitted stylesheet in web/.next/static — the guard PASSES and all eleven entries are followed by `{` or `[`, so there is no false-fail today. But `BOUNDARY` omits `.` and `&`, and nothing in the suite ever runs the check against real build output (both old and both new fixtures are built from REQUIRED_SELECTORS), so a Tailwind/Next upgrade that changes an emission shape would surface as a red build with no earlier warning.

The canary's fidelity claim — that `.grow`, `.text-right`, `.border-primary` and `.cursor-grab` canary the `client/**/*.ts` scan specifically — rests on those utilities appearing nowhere the other globs reach. Tailwind v4 extracts candidates from raw file text including comments, and the word `grow` appears in prose comments in web/app/play/TracksPopover.tsx:39 and web/app/play/PlayerShell.tsx:909, which globals.css leaves in Tailwind's automatic detection (only web/scripts/** is excluded). I could not confirm whether the extractor yields a bare `grow` candidate from `may grow:` without a build, so this is grep-only and unresolved.

The hit-area gate now mixes viewport sources: children are judged against `visualViewport.width` but the scroll ancestor's window-edge check still uses `globalThis.innerWidth`, and every vertical check still uses the equally inflatable `globalThis.innerHeight`. A popover pushed below the fold by page-level vertical overflow would pass the ancestor gate and then hand every control inside it the relaxed vertical bound that cannot fail. Not reachable today because the player is `h-dvh overflow-hidden`, so nothing inflates innerHeight.

The scroll-ancestor branch assumes the ancestor scrolls vertically only ("this ancestor only scrolls vertically, so a horizontal clip is still permanent"), but Base UI's ScrollArea viewport sets `overflow: 'scroll'` on BOTH axes (node_modules/@base-ui/react/scroll-area/viewport/ScrollAreaViewport.js:308). A control reachable only by scrolling that viewport horizontally would be failed as a permanent clip. Not reachable today — both popovers are fixed-width and their content does not overflow horizontally.

`settleToasts` now accepts opacity '0' as settled, so the hit-area position check can run against a toast mid-exit. With the current bottom-anchored Toaster (layout.tsx `offset={{ bottom: 96 }}`) sonner's exit is `translateY(100%)` (~64 px down), which stays inside the viewport; moving the Toaster to `top` would put its close button at a negative `top` and fail the position check, which carries no exemption.

The gate's stated promise is that every control "sits where a pointer can reach it", but a `pointer-events: none` control passes it. That is deliberate for this repo's aria-disabled Button pattern; the promise as written is broader than what is checked.

Finding on `dropInvalidText`'s colour coverage assumes the threat model includes a hand-edited or otherwise crafted stored document. That is the model the module states for itself (its NaN/Infinity comment), but if crafted storage is explicitly out of scope, only the whitespace finding (which the app itself used to write) remains reachable.

F4's claim that no other test covers PlayerShell's `apiValues` useMemo rests on a repo-wide text grep for `apiValues`; a guard reached through a re-export or a differently named prop would be hidden from it.

CONCEPTS.md's 'chart' ban has no CI enforcement (confirmed by review-context.md and by this lap's own finding above): the by-hand sweep that produced lap 2's A5 fix already missed a fresh instance that landed in the same file afterward. A cheap follow-up would be a case-insensitive grep gate over docs/, web/, client/ (excluding the pre-existing resources/charts/ and web/public/charts/ paths, which the project has already decided to leave alone) so this class of drift stops depending on a reviewer catching it by hand every lap.

SettingRow.tsx (new, client/src/components/ui/SettingRow/) writes its own Tailwind utility classes (h-11, min-h-11, min-w-11, w-28, w-40, w-44, etc.) directly as literal strings in the .tsx file rather than through a shared .ts class module like TrackRow/MixerClasses.ts or Slider/SliderClasses.ts. Per web/scripts/assert-design-system-css.mjs's own doc comment, a REQUIRED_SELECTORS entry is only warranted when a utility reaches the bundle EXCLUSIVELY through the '**/*.ts' scan — a .tsx-embedded class is already covered by the ordinary .tsx scan, so no new entry is owed here. Flagged only so that if these classes are later extracted into a shared .ts module (as MixerClasses.ts was for TrackRow/MasterRow), that refactor remembers to add the corresponding REQUIRED_SELECTORS entries at the same time.

I did not execute the vitest/Playwright suites myself. My assessment of both new tests this session added (the double-untick regression in player.e2e.ts and the transposition round trip against the new transposed.alphatex fixture) and of the O26 flaky-test fix is based on static reading of the mechanism plus the lap-2 triage artifact's own verification claims (mutation testing, a recorded cold-build flake that then passed four times, and a full-suite run at the lap-2 close). I reasoned through why the double-untick test's two page.evaluate() button.click() calls are genuinely synchronous within one JS task (so the race is deterministic rather than timing-dependent), and why the round-trip test's assertions read the real engine model rather than a React-state proxy, but I did not independently reproduce a red-to-green transition for either.

tooling/assert-design-system-css.mjs's BOUNDARY set (line 64) omits '\\' (backslash) as a boundary character. A REQUIRED_SELECTORS entry whose only real occurrence in a future build carried an escaped '/NN' opacity suffix (e.g. '.aria-pressed\:bg-warning\/50') would be reported as absent by isWholeClass even though the underlying utility reached the CSS in a modified form. This is not currently live — lap 2's own mutation testing confirmed all ten entries match in their bare form against the real build today — so it is a latent trap for whoever next adds an opacity-suffixed entry to that list, not a present bug.

TracksPopover.tsx's `renderLockReason` (lines 339-343, the 'At least one track must stay shown' label) reads the DISPLAY-only `drawnIndexes` (state), not `liveDrawnIndexes()`. In the same sub-16-65ms window julik-frontend-races measured and the maintainer accepted as unreachable by a human pointer (lap-2 finding O14), a second untick could in principle land with no lock reason shown, even though `applyRendered`'s own live-read guard silently no-ops the click via its `picked.length === 0` check. This is the same already-accepted, measured-unreachable race window, not a new one, so it is not raised as a finding — noted only because it is the one other read of `drawnIndexes` in a handler-adjacent position, and a future change that widens the timing window (e.g. a slower render path) would make it observable as a control that looks interactive but silently does nothing for one frame.

docs/spikes/2026-09-25-nh-291-sparse-transposition-pitches.md's 'Recommended fix' code sample (lines 328-348) differs from the shipped `setTrackTransposition` in live-settings.ts: the spike's snippet computes `-(tracks[...]?.staves[0]?.transpositionPitch ?? 0)`, which produces `-0` when the value is 0, while the shipped code explicitly guards `own === 0 ? 0 : -own` to avoid storing negative zero. This is not flagged as a finding — spike docs are dated, read-only investigation records, not living documentation, and the shipped code is a strict improvement over the spike's own suggestion — but it is worth knowing the snippet in that file no longer matches the final implementation, in case anyone re-reads the spike expecting a verbatim diff.

The TracksPopover memo() fix above is proposed from code-structural analysis (unmemoised component + a per-frame-re-rendering ancestor + already-stable props), not a live spike -- unlike O7's SettingsPopover fix, which the maintainer required to be measured before applying. TrackRow renders three Slider primitives plus per-staff toggle controls per track (client/src/components/ui/TrackRow/TrackRow.tsx, 396 lines, not itself memoised), so the true per-frame cost was not benchmarked; it likely involves fewer rows than O7's measured 90 settings rows / 71 reads (a mixer typically has a 'handful' of tracks), but each row may be structurally heavier.

TrackRow and MasterRow (client/src/components/ui/) are not memoised either. Even after wrapping TracksPopover itself in memo(), every TrackRow still receives a fresh inline closure per callback prop whenever TracksPopover re-renders from its OWN state changes (tracks/renderedIndexes/singleTrack, e.g. while the popover is open and one row is toggled), so all sibling rows still re-render together in that case. That is a separate, smaller-scope, already-present concern from the per-frame-while-closed issue this finding targets, and was not measured.

playerPositionChanged's handler (PlayerShell.tsx:417-453, unchanged by this diff) allocates a fresh closure per Player() render as the useAlphaTabEvent callback argument; this is by the hook's own documented design (a ref holds the latest handler so no resubscribe happens) and is not a material cost, but it means a future edit that adds heavier work directly inside that inline handler (rather than inside the already-coalesced rAF body) would run at the ~345/sec event rate rather than the ~60/sec frame rate -- worth a comment or lint note if it recurs elsewhere.

web/lib/player-errors.ts's cachedScoreUnavailable (E104) has no call sites anywhere in web/ (confirmed by grep across every .ts/.tsx file). It is untouched by this diff and its own comment ties it to the catalog/cached-score feature, which AGENTS.md records as paused rather than dropped, so this reads as an intentionally-reserved code rather than a defect — noted only because the brief asked to confirm every code is reachable.

loadStoredSettings's three repair passes (dropUnknownOptions, dropInvalidText, clampToBounds) all fall back to `readSettingValue(defaults, path) ?? ''` whenever a validated path is missing from `defaults`. Today every path in SETTING_OPTION_VALUES/SETTING_NUMERIC_BOUNDS/SETTING_TEXT_VALIDATORS has a matching default that itself passes its own validator (verified by hand for all 13 text rows), and the drift tests referenced in the lap-2 triage record keep the maps aligned to the descriptor tree — but nothing asserts the DEFAULT VALUES themselves stay valid. If a future edit ever adds a validated row whose default is missing or wrong, the '' fallback would very likely fail its own validator too (e.g. isFontShorthand('') is false), reproducing the 'settings were corrected' warning on every subsequent visit rather than resolving it once.

Confirmed by direct trace, not merely by reading comments: the wrong-JS-type case for a text/enum/number row (e.g. a stored number where a font string belongs) is silently absorbed by mergeAgainstDefaults with no `repaired` entry and no reset/toast — but this is an explicit, tested, documented design choice (see the 'leaves a non-string text value to the merge, which drops it without a reset' case in web/lib/alphatab/settings-storage.test.ts and its preceding comment), not a gap introduced by this diff, so it is not reported as a finding.

The first finding's reasoning that a same-score `renderScore` re-render also re-triggers `playerReady` (and therefore pushes the reset mixer state into the live audio engine, not just the UI) is inferred from PlayerShell.tsx's own comments about playerReady re-firing 'on every MIDI reload and player swap' -- it was not independently traced through AlphaTab's internal player-rebuild path to confirm it fires for a same-score re-render specifically (as opposed to only a genuine file replace or player-mode switch). If it does not, the UI-level reset (checkboxes and sliders visibly reverting) still stands on `commitTracks` alone; only the 'the audio itself reverts too' escalation would not hold.

The second finding's reentrancy trace assumes AlphaTab's event emitter dispatches listeners via a live loop, such that a listener's synchronous re-trigger of the same event runs a full nested dispatch before the outer loop continues to its remaining listeners with the original (by-then-stale) arguments.
